description: Large eagle found near water bodies. Iconic call often used to represent Africa.
Loud unmistakable call. Very common in Nairobi gardens and parks.
Famous three-note call. A sign of the rainy season in Kenya.
Black and white kingfisher. Hovers over water before diving.
Most common raptor in Nairobi. Scavenger often seen near markets.
Distinctive whining call. Common in Nairobi and dry areas.
Pairs duet together. Common in Nairobi gardens.
One of the most common garden birds in Kenya. Cheerful song.
Stunning iridescent plumage. Very common in Nairobi and Maasai Mara.
Beautiful melodious song. Common in Nairobi gardens at dawn.
Iridescent starling similar to Superb Starling but with a dark eye and orange-buff lower belly.
Small starling with striking violet-blue back in males; females are brown and streaked.
Glossy blue-green starling common in mixed flocks across East African savanna.
Glossy black starling with rufous flight feathers visible in flight. Common on buildings and cliffs.
Nomadic starling that follows locust and grasshopper outbreaks. Breeding males show bare yellow skin and wattles.
Long-tailed glossy starling with a pale iris, common in northern Kenya.
Plain grey-brown starling endemic to the East African dry savanna belt.
Glossy starling of highland forest edges and rocky escarpments, told by its slim bill.
One of Africa's most familiar doves, known for its rhythmic work-harder call.
Large reddish-brown pigeon with white-speckled wings, common on buildings and cliffs.
Small dove with iridescent green wing spots and a soft descending call.
Colonial weaver; males build elaborate woven nests and display bright yellow-and-black breeding plumage.
Small weaver with a black mask and pale eye, often nesting over water.
Highland weaver with a variable black-and-yellow head pattern, common in Nairobi gardens.
Weaver with a heavily spotted black-and-yellow back, common in colonies in dry country.
Weaver with a golden back and streaked crown, associated with papyrus and grassland edges.
Large all-golden weaver found near swamps and rivers.
Weaver with a distinctive black spectacle mask around the eyes.
Weaver with a black hood and bright yellow body, nests in reeds over water.
Small iridescent sunbird, common and widespread in gardens across East Africa.
Sunbird with a brilliant scarlet breast patch against a dark body.
Long-tailed highland sunbird with bronze-green iridescence.
Highland sunbird with a narrow scarlet breast band bordered by iridescent green and blue.
Sunbird with a small red chest patch, found near papyrus swamps and rivers.
Sunbird with a broad maroon breast band, common in drier savanna habitats.
Small green sunbird with a narrow violet collar, favors shaded forest understory.
Small sunbird with an iridescent violet back and pale underparts, found in dry bushland.
Africa's largest kingfisher, with a shaggy crest and heavy bill, found along forested rivers.
Bright blue-and-white kingfisher known for its loud trilling call, often far from water.
Small dryland kingfisher that rarely hunts near water, feeding mostly on insects.
Kingfisher with a brown head and blue-black wings, common away from water in gardens.
Kingfisher with a grey head and chestnut belly, an intra-African migrant in parts of its range.
Africa's most powerful forest eagle, preying on monkeys and small antelope; population declining with forest loss.
Distinctive eagle with a shaggy crest, often seen perched on roadside poles.
Medium-sized migrant raptor from Eurasia, present in East Africa during the northern winter.
Small pale grey-and-white raptor with red eyes, known for hovering while hunting rodents.
Small falcon known for hovering in place while scanning for prey below.
The world's fastest bird, reaching extreme speeds in its hunting stoop; found on cliffs and increasingly in cities.
Long-legged raptor with double-jointed knees, allowing it to raid nest holes for chicks and eggs.
